reports.title: Record financial results and accelerated deleveraging driven by solid operating performance and value unlocked through increased sales of gold recovered from historic concentrate stockpiles

guidance.heading: 2026 GUIDANCE
section: Consolidated copper production guidance remains unchanged at 67,500 to 77,500 tonnes, with Q4 expected to be the strongest production quarter of the year at both copper operations. At the Caraíba Operations, Q4 copper production is expected to benefit from higher mined and processed copper grades. At the Tucumã Operation, higher plant throughput and improved recoveries are expected to offset lower planned copper grades.

Full-year consolidated copper C1 cash cost(1) guidance has been updated to $2.25 to $2.45 per pound produced, reflecting the impact of continued strength in the BRL, inflationary pressures arising from the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict, and delayed access to the higher-grade pit bottom of Surubim at the Caraíba Operations during the third quarter. Unit costs are expected to decline in Q4 at both of the copper operations driven by increased production.

The cash impact of the stronger BRL has been offset by year-to-date realized gains of $30.3 million from the Company's foreign exchange hedge program. Allocating the year-to-date realized foreign exchange hedge gains across the Company's operations on a pro rata basis would translate to an estimated reduction of approximately $0.15 per pound on full-year consolidated copper C1 cash costs(1), equating to $2.10 to $2.30 per pound produced, generally in line with the Company's original 2026 guidance.

Gold from Xavantina is expected to total 75,000 to 80,000 ounces in 2026, including 30,000 to 35,000 ounces of mined production and approximately 45,000 ounces recovered from historic gold concentrate stockpiles. Mined gold production guidance has been revised to reflect extended downtime in H1 related to the installation of key ventilation and cooling infrastructure and lower mined and processed grades in Q3. Mined production is expected to increase in Q4, supported by higher mining rates and grades following the acceleration of underground development during Q3. As a result, gold C1 cash cost(1) and AISC(1) guidance has been updated to $1,650 to $1,800 per ounce and $3,300 to $3,600 per ounce, respectively. Allocating the year-to-date realized foreign exchange hedge gains across the Company's operations on a pro rata basis would translate to an estimated reduction of approximately $50 per ounce on Xavantina's full-year C1 cash costs(1) and AISC(1) equating to $1,600 to $1,750 and $3,250 to $3,550 per ounce, respectively
